text: Can you describe the characteristics of the neck swelling, such as its size, consistency, and whether it moves when you swallow? Also, have you noticed any pain, difficulty breathing, or changes in your voice?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a progressively increasing swelling on the nape of his neck for 2 months. He denies having a fever, pain, or any discharge from the swelling. He mentions a history of colon cancer for which he underwent colectomy at the age of 43. He also has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and osteoarthritis of the left knee. He takes insulin glargine, metformin, enalapril, and naproxen.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given your history of colon cancer, is this neck mass firm and fixed rather than soft and mobile? Have you noticed any weight loss, night sweats, or fatigue recently? Also, could you confirm if you have had a recent PET scan or CT of your chest/abdomen to check for metastasis?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CT Neck with Contrast reveals a well-circumscribed, hypodense lesion in the subcutaneous tissue of the nape of the neck, suggestive of a cystic nature. No evidence of invasion into underlying musculature or fixation to deeper structures. No suspicious lymphadenopathy or metastatic lesions identified in the visualized field.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Epidermoid Cyst (likely secondary to radiation or prior surgery given the colon cancer history, though metastasis is less likely given the cystic nature and lack of invasion). The imaging confirms a benign, non-invasive cystic lesion. No further immediate workup is required unless symptoms progress.
